To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the long-lived vibrational excitations in proteins are generated by the interaction of the protein side-chain residues with water molecules, which in turn interact strongly with each other through the protein-water hydrogen-bond network.

(1) the vibrational excitations in the α-helical structures are collective in nature, (2) they can be described by a nonlinear Schrödinger equation, and (3) they are excited by the interaction of side-chain residues with the water environment.

(i) a quantum dynamic model for vibrational excitations in α–helical proteins interacting with aqueous environment has been developed, and (ii) it was demonstrated that the model admits bifurcation of the solution into the weakly-damped vibrational mode and Davydov-like soliton.
